name: Midostaurin (Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis)
disease: Advanced systemic mastocytosis (ASM, SM-AHN, mast cell leukemia)
histology: advanced systemic mastocytosis: aggressive SM (ASM), SM with an associated hematologic neoplasm (SM-AHN), or mast cell leukemia (MCL)

biomarkers.KIT: midostaurin is an oral multikinase inhibitor with activity against D816V-mutated KIT; responses were seen in both KIT D816V-positive and D816V-negative/unknown patients
biomarkers.imatinibGuard: imatinib is INEFFECTIVE against KIT D816V; midostaurin (like avapritinib) retains activity against D816V. False-negative guard: imatinib is reserved for D816V-negative/unknown SM, not D816V-positive disease.
biomarkers.note: Midostaurin is FDA-approved for ASM, SM-AHN, and MCL. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Systemic Mastocytosis, SM-6 (ASM), SM-7 (SM-AHN), SM-9 (MCL), and the Discussion.

lineOfTherapy: preferred systemic therapy for advanced SM (ASM, SM-AHN, MCL); alternative to avapritinib (eg when platelets < 50 x 10^9/L preclude avapritinib)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: advanced systemic mastocytosis (ASM, SM-AHN with SM component requiring prioritization, or MCL)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, SM-6 (Preferred - Midostaurin); SM-7 (SM-AHN); SM-9 (MCL); masto lines 518, 638

drugs.name: Midostaurin

provenance.locator: Discussion MS-18 (open-label study of 116 patients with advanced SM: treatment with midostaurin 100 mg twice daily; ORR 60%); SM-6 (Preferred: Midostaurin); masto line 2883

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Systemic Mastocytosis v3.2026, Discussion MS-18 (midostaurin 100 mg twice daily for advanced SM) and SM-6 (Preferred). dosePerUnit 100 mg is the single (per-administration) dose given PO TWICE DAILY (BID) continuously; represented as days 1 to 28 of a 28-day cycle for scheduling. Total daily dose is therefore 200 mg (100 mg BID). Refer to prescribing information for dose modifications (SM-6 footnote u). Low-grade nausea/vomiting/diarrhea are the most frequent adverse events; take with food to mitigate GI toxicity per label. No ISMP tall-man form for midostaurin.

premedications.name: antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.note: Midostaurin is associated with frequent low-grade nausea/vomiting/diarrhea; give antiemetic prophylaxis and take with food per prescribing information (NCCN Systemic Mastocytosis v3.2026, Discussion MS-18).

supportiveCare: Continuous oral dosing at 100 mg twice daily; no defined cycle count - continue until progression, intolerance, or loss of response; consider allogeneic HCT evaluation on adequate response in eligible SM-AHN/MCL.
Antiemetic support and administration with food for GI tolerability.
Monitor for new/worsening cytopenias (neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia).

monitoring: CBC (grade 3-4 neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia occurred in ~24%/41%/29%)
serum tryptase and bone marrow mast cell burden (disease response)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3-4 cytopenia or intolerable GI toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume at a reduced dose per prescribing information (SM-6 footnote u); optimize antiemetics. Obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 22631 (KIT D816V is imatinib-resistant - rationale for a D816V-active agent rather than imatinib in D816V-positive advanced SM)

guideline.locator: SM-6 (ASM Preferred: Avapritinib or Midostaurin); SM-7 (SM-AHN); SM-9 (MCL); Discussion MS-18 (midostaurin 100 mg twice daily, advanced-SM open-label study, ORR 60%); masto line 2883

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for midostaurin in advanced systemic mastocytosis (ASM/SM-AHN/MCL), a rare mast-cell disorder. The dose (midostaurin 100 mg PO twice daily, continuously) is dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Systemic Mastocytosis v3.2026 Discussion MS-18 (advanced-SM open-label study) and the SM-6 Preferred recommendation; dosePerUnit is modeled as the 100 mg per-administration dose with BID captured in notes (total 200 mg/day). BIOMARKER / FALSE-NEGATIVE GUARD: midostaurin has activity against KIT D816V, unlike imatinib (DeVita line 22631); imatinib is reserved for D816V-negative/unknown SM - noted so imatinib is not mistakenly substituted for D816V-positive disease. Midostaurin is a common alternative when thrombocytopenia (< 50 x 10^9/L) precludes avapritinib. No dose is invented and no field is VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
